historical_reviews.deepseek: A short FIO match neither proves the board instance nor captures full serial/part/custom fields; naming may differ by project and the command omits a correctness oracle and Web evidence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: The passive classification is accepted. This review keeps `front-I/O` as an owner-confirmed function, distinguishes board FRU identity from front-panel controls/connectors and avoids exercising user-facing buttons or ports.
historical_reviews.related_cases: FIO I2C or hardware-function rows may share a physical assembly only after explicit mapping; their bus/functional results do not establish FRU data.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-04/34 treat board definition, topology and field values as readiness inputs; ED-38 protects logs and operator-owned result decisions.

original_test_intent: Verify the FRU identity of the project-defined FIO board, mapped to its physical panel/location and applicable interface group, and confirm the complete board-level service information matches the approved source and BMC Web.
original_method: The owner defines FIO for the platform, identifies the physical board and FRU/Web objects, supplies expected fields, then automation collects the full inventory and compares the mapped record while passively confirming that console and user-facing I/O state remain unchanged.
manual_activity: The owner confirms FIO meaning, board location and attached panel/connector scope, maps its FRU/Web records and judges field correctness. The operator need not press buttons, insert devices or alter console state for this FRU-only row.
required_inputs: Authoritative FIO meaning and physical board/panel location
Board PN/revision/serial and attached connector/control/indicator scope
Stable FRU device/area and exact BMC-Web object
Identity relation to separate FIO_BD I2C/hardware records
Approved protected IPMI access and evidence redaction
Passive console/front-I/O/BMC health baseline and recovery owner
safety_requirements: Do not infer front-I/O semantics or a physical connector map from the acronym alone
Do not reuse I2C reachability as FRU acceptance
Capture the complete inventory before exact board extraction
Do not press power/reset/UID buttons, connect media, toggle indicators or alter console/port state
Do not write FRU, flash firmware, reset BMC or clear logs
Keep credentials out of argv and preserve redacted raw output
Stop on console loss, interface-state change, duplicate/missing FRU, management instability or unexpected event
agent_execution_scope: Validate the FIO board identity and applicability
Record passive console/front-I/O and BMC health
Collect complete FRU data through approved access
Select the mapped board by stable FRU device/area and compare all required fields
Prepare the exact Web object for operator verification
Confirm no user-facing or management state changed
Perform no physical action, control write or final verdict
engineer_actions: Define FIO function/location and interface ownership
Confirm relation to other FIO source rows
Resolve identity/interface anomalies and decide the result

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The full `fru print` can supply evidence, but `grep -iA6 FIO` is a partial, name-dependent view that cannot bind a physical board, retain the full record or prove Web/spec equality. Password-bearing access is also unacceptable.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive the complete FRU inventory through approved secret-safe BMC access, select the owner-mapped FIO board by stable record identity, compare its complete required field set and correlate the exact Web object without operating panel controls or ports.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: FIO BD, `fru list`, readable/correct/Web criteria and 10/10-minute estimates remain; no acronym expansion, connector action or test stimulus is invented.

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES FIO BOARD/PANEL AND FRU FIELD MAP
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the platform's FIO assembly to its panel/location and stable FRU record, compare full board identity with service truth, verify Web parity and retain passive console/interface health solely as non-disturbance proof.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds authoritative board/panel provenance and explicitly separates FRU inspection from button, indicator and port behavior.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An FIO-labelled snippet or healthy console does not prove board FRU correctness; conversely, correct FRU data does not validate front-panel controls or port functionality.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Read-only inventory is low risk, but accidental actuation of a power/reset control or wrong FIO-board association could interrupt the host or misdirect service.

project_override_considerations: If FIO is integrated into the chassis or motherboard, identify the owning parent FRU or record not-applicable disposition. Do not invent a standalone board or silently combine functional and identity checkpoints.
expected_evidence: Exact source/variant and approved FIO meaning/location
FIO board PN/revision/serial and panel/connector ownership map
Stable FRU device/area and BMC-Web object
Complete redacted FRU output and exit status
Mapped full record with missing/duplicate/false-match analysis
Web parity and unchanged passive console/front-I/O/BMC/SEL/OS health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The row consistently requests an FIO-board FRU read and Web comparison. Undefined acronym/topology and missing values are readiness gaps rather than conflicting Master statements.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A board-level passive FRU comparison is clear after the owner supplies FIO identity and expected fields. No physical interface exercise is necessary, so the row is conditionally executable.

review_improvement: Requires FIO board-to-panel provenance, prevents unrelated functional or bus evidence from being counted and excludes potentially disruptive front-panel actuation from the FRU test.
independent_technical_reasoning: FIO may denote a front panel, a board behind it or another project-specific I/O assembly. The FRU checkpoint cannot be accepted until that label maps to a stable board record, but it also does not require touching any user-facing control. Full read-only data plus an approved field/Web oracle is sufficient; console and interface state serve only to detect unintended disturbance.
